allVisibleCapturedMeaning: true = every quest VISIBLE to this profile was captured, completed, active, failed, or listed-but-locked, across every tab the trader shows. It does NOT mean every quest the trader has: anything still gated behind an unfinished quest or an unreached loyalty level is not on screen and is therefore not here. No trader in this collection is complete in the absolute sense.

profile.note: Confirmed PvE on 2026-08-10; see the Fence batch, whose [PVE ZONE] cards carry ids that exist only in tarkov.dev's pve task list.
profile.factionNote: USEC. DETERMINED FROM THE COLLECTION ITSELF, not something written down at capture time. Four quests are faction-exclusive with no counterpart id: Road Closed (USEC), Green Corridor (BEAR), Our Own Land (BEAR) and Counteraction (USEC). "Road Closed" is ACTIVE on this profile, and the wiki says outright that it is "only obtainable by USEC PMCs" with Green Corridor as its BEAR counterpart. Both BEAR-only quests are absent from Prapor's list, which was captured in full. A BEAR profile could not show Road Closed and would have to show the other two, so the reading is unambiguous.

quests.name: Vitamins
quests.openQuestion: THE VITAMINS LINE WAS RESTRUCTURED, NOT JUST RENAMED, and the counts hide it. tarkov.dev's 'Vitamins - Part 1' is three chemical containers on Shoreline and Interchange (6 objectives); the game's 'Vitamins' is ONE container on Factory plus the respirator-and-bloodset block (also 6). Its sibling, the game's 'Supplements' (tarkov.dev 'Vitamins - Part 2', 4 objectives), is a chemical vial on CUSTOMS plus the same respirator-and-bloodset block. So the line became two parallel quests that share an item block and differ by map, and matching 6 against 6 reports agreement where the content is almost entirely different. Matched on the wiki's own page mapping (Part 1 -> Vitamins, Part 2 -> Supplements), which is the best evidence available, but the ids cannot be confirmed from a screenshot.

quests.triangleResolved: RESOLVED. The green corner triangle does NOT mean objectives are missing, it marks a page that is scrolled, which is exactly what happens when the description is scrolled out of frame to fit the list. Every card that carried it has its objective count corroborated independently: Abandoned Cargo 8 (wiki agrees), Pyramid Scheme 11 (wiki agrees, against tarkov.dev's 15), and Crisis, Aid Stations and Beneath The Streets all match tarkov.dev exactly. These captures were whole, and it shows.

quests.name: Bullshit
quests.verbatimNote: 'Roler Submariner' is the game's own in-universe brand spelling, not a transcription slip.
quests.itemChanged: RELOCATED AND REWRITTEN, and this is the FIRST case where tarkov.dev and the wiki are BOTH wrong about the map. Both describe the pre-1.1.0 quest: on CUSTOMS, stash an SV-98 sniper rifle, a Roler Submariner watch and a False flash drive in the trash by the stairs on the 3rd floor of the dorm, after first obtaining the drive, plus, per the wiki, killing no Scavs while it is active. The game's version is on LIGHTHOUSE, at the chalet tennis court, and asks for an AXMC sniper rifle, the same watch, and a MILITARY flash drive, with the obtain step and the no-kill condition gone. Map, two of three items, the drop spot and the structure all changed. A tool following either source sends the player to the wrong map with the wrong guns.

quests.objectivePinsReason: THE MATCHER PICKS THE RIGHT OBJECTIVE FOR ALL THREE AND IS OVERRULED BY THE FLOOR. Each line beats its runner-up by about 3x (0.333 vs 0.100, 0.500 vs 0.091, 0.300 vs 0.111) and two of them fall under the 0.5 absolute bar only because 1.1.0 renamed the items and moved the place, leaving almost no shared words. Loosening the bar was tried and rejected: it also paired two unrelated steps on Glory to CPSU, whose card has a line tarkov.dev does not publish at all. The find step (5c50481c…) is deliberately unpinned — the game no longer shows it, and a leftover of a type the card is not showing is kept rather than declared gone.
